messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
The test failure and the current bug report point to an issue in the method WordUtils.abbreviate(String str, int lower, int upper, String appendToEnd). The code snippet reveals how the parameters lower and upper are adjusted relative to the string length before substring operations:

1. The code first adjusts the upper bound if it is -1 or greater than the length of the string, setting it to the string length.
2. Then if upper is less than lower, upper is raised to lower.
3. However, the lower bound is never explicitly adjusted against the string length.
4. Later in the code, a substring is taken based on upper (or an index found after lower). If lower is greater than the string length, then upper can also become greater than the string length when raised to lower in line 622-623.
5. This leads to a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at line 629 or 635 when substring is called with bounds beyond the actual string length.

The bug report summary and description confirm this: lower is not adjusted when it exceeds the string length, causing upper to also become invalid and the substring call to fail. The reported fix is to limit lower to the string length to avoid this out-of-bounds error.

The failing test snippet shows a call where the lower index (15) is greater than the string length (10), matching the scenario described. Thus the test exposes this exact bug.

There are no relevant recent bug reports indicating similar adjustments, so the current evidence conclusively shows the bug arises from missing a boundary check on lower prior to substring operations in WordUtils.abbreviate.

Next, the fix should be applied to WordUtils.abbreviate to ensure lower is capped at the length of the string before it influences upper or substring calls.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
